title: Geometric series & sum to infinity
examples: When can you find the sum to infinity for a geometric series?
How do I find the number of terms needed for a sum to pass a certain value?
What does the common ratio tell me about the series?

explain.say: Today we look at geometric series and their sums. A geometric series has a constant ratio between terms.

items: A sequence where each term is multiplied by a constant ratio r.
The ratio r is found by dividing any term by the term before it.

explain.say: The common ratio r is found by dividing the second term by the first term. For example, if terms are two and four, r is two.
The sum of the first n terms is given by the formula Sn equals a times (1 minus r to the n power) divided by (1 minus r).
If the absolute value of r is less than one, the sum to infinity exists. This sum is calculated as Sinfinity equals a divided by (1 minus r).
Consider the series one plus one-quarter plus one-half-sixteen plus one-quarter-twenty-four. Here, a is one and r is one-quarter.
If you need the sum to exceed one thousand, you must solve the inequality Sn greater than one thousand for the smallest integer n.

faq.q: When can I use the sum to infinity formula?
faq.a: You can use the sum to infinity formula only when the absolute value of the common ratio r is less than one. This means that the terms get smaller and smaller.
asks: What is the condition for Sinfinity?
Does r have to be between negative one and one?

faq.q: If the ratio r is greater than one, what happens to the sum?
faq.a: If the ratio r is greater than one, the terms get larger and larger. Therefore, the sum grows without bound and does not have a finite sum to infinity.
asks: Can I find Sinfinity if r is big?

faq.q: How do I find the common ratio r if the terms are given?
faq.a: You find the common ratio r by dividing any term by the term immediately preceding it. Always check this ratio for the first few pairs of terms.
asks: If I have a sequence, how do I find r?

faq.q: What is the difference between Sn and Sinfinity?
faq.a: Sn is the sum of a fixed number of terms, n. Sinfinity is the theoretical sum if you added an infinite number of terms, provided it converges.
asks: Is Sn always smaller than Sinfinity?
When do I use Sn versus Sinfinity?

faq.q: What if the first term a is zero?
faq.a: If the first term a is zero, then every term in the series will also be zero. In this case, the sum of any number of terms is simply zero.
asks: If a=0, what is the sum?
Does the first term matter for the sum?

facts: The formula for the sum of the first n terms is Sn = a(1 - r^n) divided by (1 - r).
The sum to infinity, Sinfinity, only exists if the absolute value of the common ratio r is less than one.
If |r| < 1, the sum to infinity is calculated as Sinfinity = a divided by (1 - r).
In a geometric series, the common ratio r is found by dividing any term by its preceding term.

quiz.say: A geometric series starts with 100 and has a common ratio of one-half. What is the sum to infinity?
quiz.why: Since the ratio one-half is less than one, we use Sinfinity equals a divided by (1 minus r). This gives 100 divided by (1 minus one-half), which is 100 divided by one-half, resulting in 200.

wrong.0: This incorrectly adds the ratio to one instead of subtracting it from one for the denominator.
wrong.1: This incorrectly squares the denominator, which is not part of the sum to infinity formula.
wrong.2: This is the correct calculation, but the provided incorrect option was based on a misunderstanding of the formula setup.

quiz.say: Find the smallest number of terms, n, such that the sum of the series 3 plus 3/2 plus 3/4... exceeds 100.
quiz.why: Here a is three and r is one-half. We solve Sn greater than 100 for n. The smallest integer n that satisfies this inequality is ten.

wrong.0: You cannot use the sum to infinity because you are asked for the smallest number of terms, n, which implies a finite sum.
wrong.1: This incorrectly rearranges the inequality, forgetting the power of r in the formula.
wrong.2: This calculates the sum to infinity, ignoring the requirement to find the smallest number of terms, n.

quiz.say: For a geometric series with a first term of 5 and a common ratio of negative two-thirds, what is the sum to infinity?
quiz.why: Since the ratio negative two-thirds is between negative one and one, the sum to infinity exists. We calculate 5 divided by (1 plus two-thirds), which is 5 divided by five-thirds.

wrong.0: This incorrectly uses the formula for the sum of the first two terms instead of the sum to infinity.
wrong.2: This incorrectly uses a positive ratio when the given ratio was negative.
wrong.3: This incorrectly treats the ratio as positive two-thirds instead of negative two-thirds.
